title: 📰 AI news · November 9

items.title: Japanese store Iris Plaza leaks data of 7.7 million people
items.text: An attacker got into a third-party cloud service where Iris Ohyama kept shopper data: names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, birth dates and passwords. If your shop, bot or website keeps customer data in someone else's cloud, it sits in the same kind of place. Check who has access to the cloud holding your customers' data and close any extra doors.

items.title: Karpathy built a video site with Claude Code in 3 minutes
items.text: Andrej Karpathy released TristanTube: 47,000 videos from Tristan Hume's channel list, built in Claude Code from a single prompt in three minutes. Before that, he spent about two hours with Opus 5.5 turning 43 million Hacker News comments into HackerTube. A full service now takes an evening.

items.title: Open model Ripple-65B beats coding models 10 times its size
items.text: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview under the open Apache 2.0 license. On the agentic coding test TerminalBench 2.1 it scored 80.52, ahead of models with 501 and 816 billion parameters. It fits on the NVIDIA DGX Spark desktop machine.

items.title: Power grids worldwide dip every minute because of batteries
items.text: Researchers in Jülich found the cause of mysterious frequency dips seen in grids around the world. Backup power units and battery storage check their charge at the same moment, synced by internet clocks, so the grid sags every minute. More data centres and smart devices may make it stronger.

takeaway: Today's common thread: data and load live in other people's systems, a contractor's cloud or a shared power grid, and one weak spot reaches millions. Recommendation: list the third-party services that hold your customers' data and check who can access them.
